summary: - _e) Pass such other and further order/orders as are deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case._ - (a) The Petitioner, NHPC, has been designated as an Intermediary Procurer/ Renewable Energy Implementing Agency (REIA) for the purpose of the Act, Guidelines for Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding Process for procurement of Power from GridConnected Solar PV Power Projects. The Ministry of Power, GOI, vide resolution dated 28.07.2023, issued Guidelines for the Tariff-Based Competitive Bidding Process for Procurement of Power from Grid-Connected Solar PV Power Projects. (i) The Petitioner, NHPC, approached States/Discom(s) for providing “InPrinciple” consent for procurement of 1200 MW Power and 1200 MW under Greenshoe option through NHPC as REIA, in the above scheme. The Petitioner has yet to receive consent from the States/DISCOMs. the Petitioner shall sign the PSA with DISCOMs, and a back-to-back Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) shall be signed with the above SPGs on receiving consent from the DISCOMs/States. (j) As per clause 10.4 of Guidelines dated 28.07.2023, the Petitioner was required to file the present Petition before the Commission within 15 days of the E-Reverse Auction and hence, prayed for condonation of the delay in approaching the Commission. 3. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the submissions made in the Petition and prayed for the adoption of the tariff. Learned counsel for Respondent No. 3, i.e., Essar Renewable Limited, requested time to file the reply. 4. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels for the parties, the Petition was admitted, and notices were issued to the Respondents. The Petitioner was directed to submit the clarification, including the clause under which it has allocated 750 MW to Avada Energy Limited. 5. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that, vide affidavit dated 7.3.2025, the Petitioner has furnished the additional information/clarification sought by the Commission in the Record of Proceedings for the hearing dated 19.2.2025. Learned counsel also added that none of the Respondents has filed any reply in the matter. Learned counsel for Respondent No.3, Essar Renewable Limited, submitted that while the Respondent had initially sought liberty to file a reply, the Respondent, however, no longer wishes to file any reply in the matter. (b) _The procurer shall prepare the bid documents in accordance with the Guidelines. The principles outlined in the Guidelines may be suitable expanded and made exhaustive in the Standard Bid Documents. In case of any deviation from the provisions of the Guidelines and/or Standard Bid Documents, approval of the Appropriate Government would be necessary prior to initiation of bid process._ (k) _The PPA shall be signed with the successful bidder/ project company or an SPV formed by the successful bidder._ Committee (TEC). Per the TEC's final recommendation, seven (7) bidders were declared Petitioner, in the first round of query to the successful bidders for Greenshoe allocation, the - _10.0 All disputes arising out of and/or in connection with the selection of Solar Power Projects under the said RfS and execution of PPA thereto shall be governed by laws of India and shall be subject to the jurisdiction of Courts of Faridabad.”_ 27. Further, as per Clause 10.4 of the Guidelines dated 23.07.2023 the distribution licensee or the Intermediary Procurer, as the case may be, shall approach the Appropriate Commission for the adoption of the tariff discovered, in terms of Section 63 of the Act, within fifteen days of the discovery of the tariffs through e-RA or otherwise, in the transparent, competitive bidding process conducted in accordance with the Guidelines. In the present case, the e-RA was concluded on 09.09.2024, and accordingly, the Petitioner was required to approach the Commission for the adoption of the tariff by 24.09.2024. However, the Petitioner, NHPC, filed the present Petition only on 09.12.2024 (on the e-filing portal). In this regard, the Petitioner has submitted that the tariff was discovered by way of e-Reverse Auction on 09.09.2024; thereafter, the Standing Tender Committee constituted in accordance with the Bidding Guidelines, evaluated the bids and prices discovered in the e-reverse auction as per the requirement of the Bidding Guidelines, and recommended the issuance of the LoAs to the successful bidders, i.e., Respondents herein. Pursuant to the recommendation, approval was granted by the Competent Authority for awarding the selected project capacity to the Selected Bidders (i.e., the Respondents herein) on 09.10.2024. Accordingly, the Petitioner was obligated to approach this Commission to adopt the tariff by 24.09.2024. The Petitioner further submitted that the time taken for requisite approvals was unavoidable. Soon after issuance of the LOAs, the Petitioner completed all activities involved in filing the Petition, including preparing the Petition, compiling relevant documents, and processing the filing fees, in the shortest possible time. The Petitioner also submitted that a request has been made to the MNRE vide letter dated 25.05.2024, GOI to review the requirement of filing the Petition for the adoption of tariff within 15 days of E-Reverse Auction, and also requested 60 days after signing of the PPA/PSA for approaching the Appropriate Commission for the adoption of tariff. The Petitioner has submitted that, at the request of various REIAs, the MNRE is actively considering making the needful changes. Due to surplus solar power and DISCOMs' reluctance to buy it, NHPC was able to obtain consent from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra. According to the Petitioner, the delay in filing the Petition was due to the time required to comply with the transparent competitive bidding guidelines dated 23.07.2023. 42.
